pr_title: Add VWAP and STD execution models
pr_body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
Creates two new execution models. First, `VolumeWeightedAveragePriceExecutionModel` will submit market orders while the price is more favorable than VWAP. Second, the `StandardDeviationExecutionModel` will submit market orders when the current price is at least the specified number of deviations away from the mean. Both models accept an implementation of `IOrderSizingStrategy` which is used to break up the order into multiple orders. Two implementations of `IOrderSizingStrategy` are also provided: `PercentVolumeOrderSizingStrategy` which defines a maximum order size as a specified percentage of volume from the current bar and the `TotalValueOrderSizingStrategy` which defines a maximum order size using a specified maximum order value.

Continuing to fill out the algorithm framework models namespace, providing some default models for users to use.

pr_comments:
The `StandardDeviationExecutionModel` aims to submit market orders when the price is a certain number of standard deviations away from the mean. So for buy orders, it waits for price to go below `SMA + c*STD`, and for sell orders it would wait for price to go above `SMA + c*STD`. Equally for the math inclined: `μ ± cσ`, where `c` is the number of standard deviations away from the mean. Additionally, it will break up orders by value, configurable by the `MaximumOrderValue` property, which defaults to $20,000.

Here's a view of `StandardDeviationExecutionModel` in action. The lines are:
```
Orange: SMA(60min) + 2*STD(60min)
Pink:   SPY(min)
Blue:   SMA(60min)
Green:  SMA(60min) - 2*STD(60min)
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/531416/38440335-21c6e0d2-39af-11e8-94c3-1dd95b5e8724.png)

The model was asked to make a sell order for SPY at 1:00PM, but waited until 1:08PM when the price moved at least 2 standard deviations away from the mean before submitting market orders. In addition, this model was configured to submit orders with a maximum order value of $20k, hence the multiple orders, one each minute:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/531416/38440293-f94a3244-39ae-11e8-90e4-dbbd918a0f43.png)

Now, it wasn't done reaching it's target yet, so you can see later in the chart the price moves favorably again and we actually ended up submitting a market on open order for tomorrow at the close:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/531416/38440459-8208507a-39af-11e8-884a-ac1fc1e09e23.png)

Note for future; normally with equities it is aiming to meet or better the VWAP for _day_ - so we could make it submit an order for any remaining quantity as a MOC order at 15.45 before MOC cut off. 

Those commit messages are great thank you. 

Whole PR TLDR; Pending problem we need to solve: given most people work/think in currency pairs (BTCUSD) - how do we intuitively & automatically create portfolios from alpha signals and execute on them.   For now handled as margin models and orders will get bounced.

The `VolumeWeightedAveragePriceExecutionModel` aims to submit market orders when the price is more favorable than the current VWAP. This differs from a broker's VWAP execution in that they typically guarantee your order will fill (within some size limits) and that you'll receive at-or-better than VWAP by end of the day. This algorithm is much simpler in that it will only submit orders when the price is more favorable than the current VWAP.

Here's a view of the `VolumeWeightedAveragePriceExecutionModel`. The lines are:
```
Orange: IBM(min)
Green:  VWAP(IBM)
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/531416/38444205-6cd6ba40-39bc-11e8-90d7-702df4120be7.png)
You can see the model executing sell orders while the price is great than the current VWAP. It then stops when the price falls, and when it rallies back above VWAP it begins selling again. In addition, the model breaks up an order based on the current bar's trading volume. You can set the `MaximumOrderQuantityPercentVolume` on the model to change the percentage of the current bar's trading volume used as the maximum order size. This value defaults to 1% => `0.01m`.

Interesting to note that this is all the execution model reacting to a single $1MM IBM sell order.

issue_context.title: Create VWAP Execution Model
issue_context.body:
<!--- This template provides sections for bugs and features. Please delete any irrelevant sections before submitting -->

#### Description
Create a new `VwapExectionModel`. We'll define VWAP execution as placing market orders while the security's current price is below the current VWAP. A parameter should be provided that is used to determine the maximum size of each order submitted, ideally leveraging the security's current trading volume as a measure of market depth in place of having access to order book data.

review_comments: Later we can add a history call here to warm up the indicators
Future me: `!member.HoldStock .... member.Holdings.Target.Quantity == 0` no holdings and not aiming for any more.
Wonder if we can reuse the PreOrderChecks method. Wonder if these will grow over time

There's another flag, `IsTradable` -- currently only a public get/set and we use it to set internal feeds to false, I could see it being a little smarter and also returning false when price is zero, and perhaps other things we may check (assuming they relate directly to the security, ofc)
Note: we realize this could potentially never be 0 if you're trading cross pairs; as the portfolio.Quantity and cashbook[coin].Quantity will be incompatible. WIP until resolve how to model better.
Included in that thought experiment should be consideration for what a portfolio target against a pair means without the concept of virtual positions?
